tasks.name: Tarasq
tasks.description: This athletic movement was originally designed to mimic a baseball player fielding a baseball with his/her glove and having to a throwing position. The short description: Alternate your lower about roughly 180 degrees using a "pop turn" that's generated from your front leg. Always touch the turf on each jump. Use your front/leading hand to touch the turf and always touch in the inside step of your front foot. Detailed: Assumed a half-squat position  with your feet in a Squonq position (back foot parallel to line 1, front foot turned nearly 90 degrees open  towards the field.) Bend and the knees and hip to touch the turf on the inside step of the front foot. Jump forward using primarily the lead leg while simultaneously turning 180 degrees and landing in the same Squonq stance, but now with the opposite foot  open towards the field. Proceed to touch the turf with your other  hand this time and continue in this manner, alternating "pop turns" and touches until you reach the end zone. Watch for incorrect hinging JUST at the hips and zero bend at the knee, this will alleviate any back discomfort. As you learn the rhythm  you'll find that during the touch (with your hand) that your weight will be more on the back leg and as you jump and transition into the turn the weight is transferred into the front leg.

tasks.name: Tarasq
tasks.description: This athletic movement was originally designed to mimic a baseball player fielding a baseball with his/her glove and having to a throwing position. The short description: Alternate your lower about roughly 180 degrees using a "pop turn" that's generated from your front leg. Always touch the turf on each jump. Use your front/leading hand to touch the turf and always touch in the inside step of your front foot. Detailed: Assumed a half-squat position  with your feet in a Squonq position (back foot parallel to line 1, front foot turned nearly 90 degrees open  towards the field.) Bend and the knees and hip to touch the turf on the inside step of the front foot. Jump forward using primarily the lead leg while simultaneously turning 180 degrees and landing in the same Squonq stance, but now with the opposite foot  open towards the field. Proceed to touch the turf with your other  hand this time and continue in this manner, alternating "pop turns" and touches until you reach the end zone. Watch for incorrect hinging JUST at the hips and zero bend at the knee, this will alleviate any back discomfort. As you learn the rhythm  you'll find that during the touch (with your hand) that your weight will be more on the back leg and as you jump and transition into the turn the weight is transferred into the front leg.

tasks.name: Tarasq
tasks.description: This athletic movement was originally designed to mimic a baseball player fielding a baseball with his/her glove and having to a throwing position. The short description: Alternate your lower about roughly 180 degrees using a "pop turn" that's generated from your front leg. Always touch the turf on each jump. Use your front/leading hand to touch the turf and always touch in the inside step of your front foot. Detailed: Assumed a half-squat position  with your feet in a Squonq position (back foot parallel to line 1, front foot turned nearly 90 degrees open  towards the field.) Bend and the knees and hip to touch the turf on the inside step of the front foot. Jump forward using primarily the lead leg while simultaneously turning 180 degrees and landing in the same Squonq stance, but now with the opposite foot  open towards the field. Proceed to touch the turf with your other  hand this time and continue in this manner, alternating "pop turns" and touches until you reach the end zone. Watch for incorrect hinging JUST at the hips and zero bend at the knee, this will alleviate any back discomfort. As you learn the rhythm  you'll find that during the touch (with your hand) that your weight will be more on the back leg and as you jump and transition into the turn the weight is transferred into the front leg.

tasks.name: Scalawag
tasks.description: Like Rev Gremlin and Crook but with Squonq feet. Position the feet with a sqounq base, point the TRAILING toe towards the end zone that you're leaving, LEAD foot should be parallel to the turf-lines. Move backwards SLOWLY with your LEAD foot first, then follow behind with the TRAILING foot. Be sure to rotate to face the other direction at the far end zone so that you'll have the other leg pointing to endzone on the way back. This task was designed to get people to slow down on Squonq and understand the footwork.
